source_en: Evening performance at the Rustaveli Theatre.
Home after a late rehearsal.
Costume fitting in the theatre district.
Sunday lunch with my parents.
Typing pool shift. I could never act.
My husband's birthday, with his family.
Don't mind the mask. Old scars. Nothing interesting.
You have a very serious expression. I find that attractive.
My papers are ready. I was here yesterday. Remember?
The mask is part of my face. It stays.
Good instincts, Officer. I will remember that.
I will need to contact someone. One moment.
You will hear from people I know. I say that calmly.
The mask... stays on... even now...
You could have... just looked away...
Where are you coming from?
Rehearsal at the Rustaveli. Three of us, playing to empty seats.
My mother's flat in Rustavi. She cooks for me every Sunday.
I was already here. Before you sat down.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
Nothing. The mask covers old scars, not fever. Stop staring.
Nothing. The mask is for show. At home, it's off.
No. Ask again. The answer will still be no.
You keep staring. Most people have manners.
The family section is blank on purpose. Note it down.
